doc.title: Ray Shiner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 1998

title: Dorothy Jarnac's dance career
summary: Stopette commercial, Lili, Broadway shows, and Lebanese food.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: I’m curious, you know there’s now with so many cable channels they have the T.V. Land station and they have these, they call them retro commercials, they’re showing some of the old commercials. I’m wondering if you ever hear yourself?
Well I’ll tell you what I will see is probably my wife dancing. She did one of the first Stopette commercials, just a dialogue, no music, just talk.
Stopette. The original — see you’re young — it’s an original deodorant. Stopette was one of the original deodorants.

Dorothy Jarnac was her professional name, and she would come out and the announcer would go through this copy and she would do the copy by walking. She was on the Peter Lind Hayes Show. She was on many shows. She was on concert stage.
Wouldn’t that be something to see that.

Oh, I wish they had videos of my wife dancing. Well she was in a movie. She did “Lili” she was the barn puppet in the movie “Lili,” and she was in several Broadway shows, the Bluerville brought her to New York. She did “Ticket Squeeze,” oh she was a world famous dancer. She was in Life Magazine twice.
Well it’s no wonder you two were attracted to each other, being into art and Lebanese food.
The Lebanese food, which is what did it, which kills me. I’m Lebanese and my wife was a mixture of Irish, German, English, Spanish, a little French, everything. But she liked Lebanese food.
